confirmed.title: Round-9 'own ground' buried check also applies to the main building's own parts: a part lying wholly below the building's grade plane is no longer stopped, and the height shows a negative reading
confirmed.detail: With spot grades, _ground_against now marks a solid 'above the ground' when its top is above the LOWEST corner of its own ground (min(ground_for)). The height and stories still measure from the building's grade plane. So a part of the main building that sits wholly below the grade plane but reaches above its own downhill corner is let through. Before a0cbb56 this was the buried_solid stop. Now the height is measured from the grade plane with that part's roof as the 'main roof', which gives a negative height reading. Reproduced: lower=box(10,25,35,65,-6,-2,'low'), upper=box(10,25,35,45,-2,30,'up'), spots [[22.5,24.5,-6],[22.5,65.5,0],[35.5,35,-1],[35.5,55,0],[9.5,35,-1],[9.5,55,0]], ground_is_flat None, grade_elevation None. The grade plane is -1.333. At HEAD, building_height readings are 'leaving out what rises above the main roof; a flat roof, to its highest level' = -0.666667 and 'including ...' = 31.333333. Stories says 'part of the building (low) is below the ground', so stories judges the same part as below grade while the buried check judges it as above. building_area and the yards come out as values (1000 sf, rear 35). At 304e9e6 every one of these was 'a solid lies wholly under the ground (-1.333333 ft; it runs from -6.0 to -2.0 ft)'. It is not a false pass, because the checker needs every reading to pass and the 31.33 reading is still there. But architects are shown a below-zero building height, and one building is now read against two different ground levels: the buried check uses its own lowest corner, the height and stories use the grade plane.
confirmed.evidence: level[b["id"]] = min(ground) if ground else grade ... joined = {i for i, (lo_, hi_) in spans.items() if hi_ > at(i) + TOL or hi_ - lo_ <= TOL}; while _height(main, grade) and _stories_whole (`low = [b for b in plain if _extent(b)[0] < grade - TOL]`) use the grade plane. _measure: `_ground_against(buildings, grade, off_check=not spots, points=spots)` with no restriction to other buildings.
confirmed.pin: New test in packages/model_measurement/tests/test_measure.py with the lower/upper/spots above. It asserts that building_height has no reading below 0, and either that the record carries the buried_solid stop or that every reading is at least the grade-plane height. It fails at a0cbb56: the -0.666667 reading is present.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Read a solid on its own ground (ground_for) only when it is a different building from the one whose grade is given, i.e. not in the same _connected group or stack as the grade's building. Judge the parts of the grade's own building against `grade`, as before round 9. In _measure that building is the main building's group; in _candidate_grades it is the candidate's members. The shed in test_a_short_shed_on_its_own_lower_ground_is_never_buried_under_the_houses_grade is a separate group, so it keeps working.

confirmed.title: The ground cut for the MAIN building is now the average ground at its face corners, not the §325-3 grade plane: 'at the main grade level' and the yards' 'walls at ground level' are cut at a different level than the height uses
confirmed.detail: Round 9 replaced plan_level with `level = sum(ground)/len(ground)` for every solid that has its own spot grades, the main building included. That number is the fitted, clamped plane averaged over every face vertex, with each corner counted once per face it belongs to. It is not §325-3's 'average of finished ground level on each side of the building at exterior walls', which grade_plane computes and which the height still uses. When the ground is not a plane, or vertices are spread unevenly, the two differ, and the cut lands on the wrong floor. Reproduced: lower=box(10,25,35,45,-6,-2,'low'), upper=box(10,25,35,65,-2,30,'up'), same spots as the finding above. grade_plane = -1.333, which is the height's base (31.333). The vertex mean is -2.153, so the cut falls in the lower block. At HEAD, building_area reads 'at the main grade level' = 500 against 'covered from above' = 1000, which raises the overhang question. rear_yard 'to its walls at ground level' = 55 against 35, which raises the yard question. At 304e9e6, cutting at the grade plane gave 1000/1000 and 35/35, both values. With the vertical order swapped the opposite happens: the cut falls below the grade plane and a real overhang question disappears. The main building's own cut should never have moved. The prior finding was only about other buildings (a shed on its own lower ground).
confirmed.evidence:

... return _section(building, max(level, bottom) + TOL)
while `plan_level = grade if grade_known else lo` (grade = grade_plane(...)), and the reading is labelled 'at the main grade level'. ground_for's corners = [p[:2] for b in buildings for f in b.get("faces") or [] for p in f["points"]] (every face vertex, duplicates included).
confirmed.pin: New test with lower=box(10,25,35,45,-6,-2), upper=box(10,25,35,65,-2,30) and the spots above. It asserts that the building_area reading 'at the main grade level' == 1000 (the section at grade_plane -1.333) and that rear_yard has value 35. It fails at a0cbb56: the reading is 500 and the rear yard is a question.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Keep cutting the main building, and any solid in its _connected group, at plan_level (the grade plane). For another building with spot grades of its own, cut at its own grade plane by the same §325-3 function (_grade_from_points([b], points, others)), not at a vertex-weighted average of the plane. When that function refuses, fall back to the current rule (max(ground) and its bottom).
skeptics:
I read packages/model_measurement/model_measurement/measure.py:185-207 (_at_ground), 1114-1120 (ground_for: corners = every face vertex, duplicates included), 1091-1099 (_ground_at: a fitted plane clamped to the spot range), 1154-1196 (grade_plane / _grade_from_points: the average of the walls' averages), and the callers at 1383 (building_area 'at the main grade level') and 1411-1413 (yards 'to its walls at ground level'). Commit a0cbb56 (round 9) changed `_section(building, max(plan_level, bottom)+TOL)` to `max(level, bottom)`, with `level = sum(ground)/len(ground)` whenever the solid has its own spot grades. It does this for every solid, the main building included, while plan_level = grade_plane (line 1275) is still what the height uses. So this change is new in the branch, not something already on origin/start-project.

I reproduced it with the venv Python and the test helpers. lower=box(10,25,35,45,-6,-2,'low'), upper=box(10,25,35,65,-2,30,'up'), and a random search for spot grades that put grade_plane above -2 and the vertex mean below it. Result: grade_plane = -1.878, and building_height = 31.878 uses that grade. The cut, though, reads building_area [covered from above 1000, at the main grade level 500] and rear_yard [seen from above 35, walls at ground 55], so both turn into review questions. Cutting at the grade plane (-1.878) would land in the upper block and give 1000 and 35.

Calling _at_ground on each solid by itself gives up=1000 and low=0, so the 500 must come from the stacked solids being read as one merged main solid. Its vertex-averaged ground (-2.30) falls in the lower block, below the §325-3 grade plane. The finding is correct: the main building's ground cut now uses a different level than the grade plane the height uses. In this direction it gives 'needs review' instead of a value, so it is not a false pass. The reverse order, which would hide a real overhang question, follows from the same code path, but I did not run it.

The finding holds. I read packages/model_measurement/model_measurement/measure.py:185-207 (_at_ground), 1114-1120 (ground_for), 1154-1196 (grade_plane / _grade_from_points) and the two callers at 1383 (building_area) and 1411-1413 (the yards' "to its walls at ground level").

What the code does: whenever ground_for returns ground for a solid, line 203 sets `level = sum(ground)/len(ground)`, and that applies to the main building as well. ground_for (line 1118) builds its corners from every face vertex, so shared corners are counted more than once, and it reads them off the fitted, clamped spot-grade surface. That is not _grade_from_points' §325-3 average of wall averages, which is the base the height uses. `git diff 304e9e6 HEAD` confirms that round 9 (a0cbb56) brought this in: the old code cut at `max(plan_level, bottom)` for every solid.

Reproduced with the repo's .venv. I used the finding's two blocks: lower = box(10,25,35,45,-6,-2) and upper = box(10,35,35,65,-2,30), which _stacks merges into a single main building. My spot grades were: front -6, back 0, side spots -3 at y=30, -1.5 at y=40 and 0 at y=55. The results:
- grade_plane = -1.875, and building_height = 31.875, so the height starts at the grade plane.
- The vertex mean = -2.117, so the cut falls into the lower block.
- building_area readings: [1000, 500].
- rear_yard readings: [35, 55] (the ground-level wall reading is at y=45, the lower block's rear wall).

When the spots make the grade plane and the vertex mean agree (for example -1.25), the readings come back [1000, 750] and [35, 35]. So the divergence comes from using the vertex mean instead of the grade plane.

One detail differs from the finding: in my case a cut at the grade plane would give 750 for area, not 1000, so the area question would still be raised there. The rear-yard question, however, only appears because of the vertex mean. Either way, the main building is cut at a different level from the one the height uses. The code path is reachable in normal use: the main building with its own spot grades. I found no upstream guarantee that keeps the two levels equal. _at_ground does not exist on origin/start-project; the change is new on this branch, from 304e9e6 to HEAD.

priorStatus.title: The buried-solid check still judges every building against the main house's grade plane, not ground_for: a short outbuilding on its own lower ground stops building area, yards and height
priorStatus.reasoning: The fix is in a0cbb56. _ground_against now reads each solid on its own ground (ground_for, with pool = every building in _candidate_grades and the default pool elsewhere). _at_ground cuts a resting solid at its own ground. I ran the reported case: there is no 'wholly under the ground' reason, building_area is 680/680, and envelope_grade returns (0.0, None). With a north-wall spot added for the shed, the height comes out as readings 30/33 (the accessory question), not a stop. The test pin fails if the change is reverted, and the 'lost' solid with no spot grades of its own is still refused. The fix also reaches parts of the main building itself, which causes two new P2 regressions, reported separately: a negative height reading, and the main building's cut moving off the grade plane. The full model_measurement suite passes (226 passed).
